g: A personal computer, especially one similar to an IBM PC that runs Microsoft Windows (or, originally, DOS), usually as opposed to (say) an Apple Mac.
(Canadian politics, by extension) A member of the Conservative Party of Canada.
(bingo) forty-nine (an allusion to a cartoon character, Police Constable 49)
(sometimes with up) To make politically correct.
1991 December, Renée Gearhart Levy, “PC’ed Out,” Syracuse University Magazine, quoted in Steven Mailloux, Reception Histories, Cornell University Press (1998), →ISBN, page 169.
(South Korea) A public internet cafe where people can meet to play multiplayer computer games for a fee.

(computing) A removable memory or I/O device that fits into an expansion slot on a notebook computer or a personal digital assistant (PDA). PC Cards are used primarily in notebook computers and PDAs. PC Card peripherals include Wi-Fi network cards, memory cards, modems, wired NICs, and hard drives.
Synonym of personal computer (“a PC-compatible computer”)
(South Korea) Nationwide computer networks that preceded the World Wide Web/Internet, with telnet-based dial-up connections and bulletin board messaging systems.
(UK, informal, derogatory) A policeman (implying that he is dull and slow).
(Internet slang, politics) An act in which a user intimidates or harasses another into changing their personal opinions because they do not consider them politically correct enough.
(computing) A device found in most IBM PC compatible computers that allows simple beeps to be output.
(computing, historical) Of a computer, offering the compatibility of the IBM Personal Computer regarding software, and―to a lesser degree―hardware.
(informal) One who uses a personal computer.
(molecular biology) A plasmid containing the cytomegalovirus (CMV) immediate-early promoter
To perform a polymerase chain reaction.
